observation.visible_scene: A pink, rose/swirl-shaped wax candle with a burning wick sits centered inside a metal cup that has a handle on its right side; the cup rests on a flat black surface. A vertical dark metal rod stands behind the cup against a plain white wall, with pale green surfaces visible at the left and right edges. A pool of melted pink wax surrounds the base of the candle within the cup. The flame is present from the first frame and remains lit through the last.
visible_changes: The candle flame flickers continuously throughout the clip, varying in height, width, brightness and tilt from frame to frame.
The flame alternately leans to the right, to the left, or stands nearly vertical; at several moments (e.g. mid-clip) it stretches tall and tilts rightward toward the background rod.
The candle body, the wick stub, the melted-wax pool and the cup/handle/rod positions remain essentially fixed; the only pronounced motion is the flame's shape and orientation.
No camera movement is evident: the cup, handle, background rod and wall keep constant positions across frames, so the apparent changes are flame flicker rather than viewpoint shift.
outside_clip_unknowns: What caused the air movement producing the flicker, and whether the flame will go out or the candle will melt down further, are not shown.
The exact start of the burning and any later outcome lie outside this cropped segment.
Whether the melted pool grows over a longer time cannot be judged from this short excerpt.
uncertain_details: The wax and wick material identities are not verifiable from the images.
Any very slow change in the candle's height or the pool's extent is too subtle to confirm over this interval.
The wick's slight apparent shape differences between frames may be flicker/occlusion by the flame rather than real deformation.
